assumptions.value: Alluvial groundwater wellfield up the fan, 2,186,952 m3/yr fresh in phase one (about 69 L/s); 1,412,340 m3/yr more is reclaimed wastewater
assumptions.basis: No water right is supplied by the organiser and recharge is unknown, so phase two is gated on measured drawdown rather than on a yield we cannot know.

assumptions.value: 40 MW: two 20 MW halls; pads for two more reserved on the terrace for phase two
assumptions.basis: Sized so that the PV and storage can carry the city first and the campus second, islanded.

assumptions.value: No grid connection in phase one; the city runs as an islanded microgrid
assumptions.basis: Grid capacity is not supplied; the nearest road (RN 20) is 40.7 km beyond the site and no transmission line is assumed.

assumptions.value: Dry coolers with adiabatic assist above 35 C (about 500 h/yr): WUE 0.20 L/kWh, PUE 1.25
assumptions.basis: Water binds, power does not; dry cooling gives up about 0.1 of PUE to save most of the water. WUE per IT kWh.

assumptions.value: 2,150 kWh/kWp/yr, single-axis tracking, 2 ha per MWp
assumptions.basis: Order of magnitude for the high-irradiance Andean piedmont at 31.1 S; to be replaced by a PVGIS run (S-01).

assumptions.value: 1,000 MWh lithium iron phosphate, round-trip efficiency 88%
assumptions.basis: Carries the city's night load (about 15 MW) and the campus at 70% for 13 hours with margin.

assumptions.value: 100% physical hourly carbon-free supply; the city is served first; compute available 85% of hours at full load
assumptions.basis: Day: 11 h at full load. Night: 13 h at 70% from storage. Winter cloud: batch work curtailed. 11 x 100% + 13 x 70% = 84% of full-load hours.

assumptions.value: 130 L per person per day; 80% returns as wastewater; 90% of it reused
assumptions.basis: Metered supply, greywater separation and low-flow fittings in an arid new city; San Juan's own consumption is far higher and is not the benchmark.

assumptions.value: Orchards 226 ha at 4,000 m3/ha/yr deficit drip; greenhouses 14 ha at 8,000; north terrace 338 ha of jojoba and algarrobo at 600 (establishment); irrigated streets, patios and squares 50 ha at 6,000; industry 60,000 m3/yr
assumptions.basis: Orchards and street trees run on reclaimed water through the acequias; the river park, north slope and PV fields are unirrigated desert planting.

assumptions.value: 85 m2 gross per dwelling; 2.4 persons per dwelling; mixed-use blocks two thirds residential
assumptions.basis: Courtyard houses and flats of 55-120 m2 for a young city with families.

assumptions.value: 7891 jobs located in the city: Compute campus operations and security 140; PV, batteries and the microgrid 120; Greenhouses 141; Orchards, acequias and landscape crews 420; Agri-processing, cold store and packing 260; Workshops: PV and robot maintenance for the whole site's fields, fabrication, repair 900; Freight cross-dock and autonomous fleet 220; Water reclamation and the bluff tank 60; Schools 790; Kindergartens and health posts 420; Clinic 260; Training college (robotics, agronomy, water) 180; Town hall, open-data office and administration 280; Library, culture, media school 120; Markets, shops, cafes and food 2200; Arrival hall, guesthouse and visitors 260; Personal and home care 700; Lead-zone field operations living in the city 420
assumptions.basis: Staffing ratios per facility; the construction workforce of phase two is temporary and excluded.

assumptions.value: Zonda from the west to north-west, hot and dry, several days a year; ordinary winds not assumed
assumptions.basis: Wind data is not supplied; to be checked against SMN San Juan Aero observations before phase two.

assumptions.value: Greenhouse night heating about 1.2 GWh/ha/yr; hot water for the civic quarter and the market about 8 GWh/yr: about 25 GWh of about 300 GWh IT energy
assumptions.basis: The campus is 2.4 km from the nearest homes, so heat goes only to the greenhouses beside it and, by an insulated main down the bluff, to the civic quarter.

assumptions.value: Highest seismic zone of INPRES-CIRSOC 103 assumed; buildings of six floors or fewer, most of two to four; regular, short-span courtyard blocks in reinforced concrete frames or confined masonry
assumptions.basis: San Juan is among the most seismically active provinces; edition and zone to be confirmed (S-03).

assumptions.value: Four oasis cities of about 40,000 each on the Line, about 160,000 people
assumptions.basis: Each city stays within a 2.5 km walk across and within reach of its own wellfield; size is limited by water, not land.

assumptions.value: combined: separated on the 600 m machine grid; shared at walking pace on the acequia streets; people only in the lanes
assumptions.basis: Freight and shuttles never need the lanes; doorstep delivery uses the acequia streets; every crossing of a machine street is a marked interface.

assumptions.value: About 153 GWh/yr for the city (2,000 kWh per resident plus 70 GWh non-residential), 372 GWh/yr for the campus at PUE 1.25
assumptions.basis: All-electric city with heat pumps and an electric fleet; to be replaced by an hourly load model.

assumptions.value: The lower terrace stands 4-15 m above the wash bed and outside the DEM flood-sensitive band; storm water from the bluff is led round the city in two swales to the river park
assumptions.basis: Flood peaks are not supplied; the city is placed out of the band instead of being raised inside it.
